config.title: Children Prop

intro.title: Children Prop
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that accepts and displays content passed to it from a parent component. You will learn how to use the special 'children' prop, which allows components to wrap and render any JSX elements or text you place between their opening and closing tags. This lesson focuses on TypeScript in React, showing you how to properly type the children prop for type safety. By the end, you'll understand how to create flexible, reusable components that can nest other content.
intro.usecase: The children prop pattern is fundamental for building reusable UI components in real-world React applications. You'll see this pattern in dashboard layouts where sidebar panels, content areas, and widget containers wrap different content while maintaining consistent styling and behavior. It's essential for creating flexible navigation menus, modal dialogs, and card components that can display varied content without modifying the container component itself. This approach allows developers to create maintainable design systems where container components define structure and styling, while content remains completely customizable.

objectives: Implement a React component that accepts and renders children using the children prop
Apply TypeScript type annotations to properly type the children prop in functional components
Construct nested component structures by passing JSX elements as children
Manipulate children content by wrapping it with additional markup or styling
Initialize and render components with varying child content types (text, elements, components)
Integrate the children prop with other component props to create flexible UI elements
Configure components to conditionally render children based on component state or props

steps.title: Import React and ReactNode
steps.instruction: Import React and the ReactNode type from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and ReactNode from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a module
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, making React and ReactNode available for use.
successCriteria: React and ReactNode are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and ReactNode from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and ReactNode from 'react'.

steps.title: Create a Card component with typed children prop
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Card that accepts a children prop typed as ReactNode and returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define the component with an interface for props that includes children: ReactNode, then implement the component body.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { ReactNode } from 'react';

// Create your Card component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Card component is defined with proper TypeScript typing for the children prop.
successCriteria: Card component is created with an interface/type for props that includes children: ReactNode, and the component returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your Card component accepts children as a prop with ReactNode type and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component isn't defined correctly. It should accept children typed as ReactNode and return null.

steps.title: Add basic structure to Card component
steps.instruction: Inside your Card component, return a div element with the className 'card' that renders the children prop.
steps.hint: The children prop should be placed inside the div's opening and closing tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Card component returns a div with the class 'card' that wraps around the children prop.
successCriteria: The Card component returns a div element with className 'card' and renders the children prop inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div with className 'card' and placing the children prop inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Card component should return a div element with className 'card' that renders the children prop. Check your return statement and JSX structure.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called App that returns <> </>.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an App component ready to be filled with content in later steps.
successCriteria: App component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named App that returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not correctly defined. Check the component name and return statement.

steps.title: Use Card component with text content as children
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, render the Card component and pass a string of text as its children prop.
steps.hint: Place the text content directly between the opening and closing tags of the Card component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component renders a Card component containing text content passed as children.
successCriteria: The Card component is rendered inside App with text content between its tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're rendering the Card component inside App and placing text between its opening and closing tags.
steps.feedbackWrong: The goal is to render the Card component with text content as children inside the App component.

steps.title: Create a Button component with typed children prop
steps.instruction: Create a new functional component named Button that accepts a children prop typed as ReactNode.
steps.hint: Define the component below the Card component, using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember to include the typed children parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Button component is defined with proper TypeScript typing for its children prop.
successCriteria: Button component is created with a children prop typed as ReactNode.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a Button component, but check that the children prop is properly typed as ReactNode.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component is missing or doesn't have the correct children prop typing.

steps.title: Add button structure and styling
steps.instruction: Inside the Button component, add a button element with className 'btn' that renders the children prop.
steps.hint: The button element should be returned from the Button component, using the children prop as its content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Button component will render a button element with the 'btn' class, displaying whatever content is passed as children.
successCriteria: Button component returns a button element with className 'btn' that renders the children prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a button element with className 'btn' that uses the children prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component should return a button element with className 'btn' that renders the children prop.

steps.title: Use Button component with text and icons as children
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a Button component with text and emoji icons as children. For example: 'Click me 🚀🌟'
steps.hint: Pass a string containing both text and emojis as the children prop to the Button component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: passing mixed content as children
<Button>Submit ✅</Button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component renders a Button with text and emoji icons as its children content.
successCriteria: Button component is used with text and emoji icons passed as children prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're passing both text and emoji icons as children to the Button component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Button component should receive text and emoji icons as its children prop.
